The corpus it scores was sealed two commits earlier at H-PRE, before any checker existed.

sealed_commit_note: The H-PRE commit that sealed experiments/house_rules_fixtures.json before scripts/symbol_ledger.py existed. B10 requires the run artifact to cite it and requires it to be an ancestor of the scoring tip; the runner proves that with git merge-base --is-ancestor and records the proof.
declared_output_paths_note: DESIGN §6.3 fixes these as EXACTLY two and calls them the complete B4 exclusion list. B4 compares write_stage.working_tree_digest before and after the run excluding them; nothing else may appear.
outputs_name_no_admitted_symbol_note: A construction rule this registration adopts so B5 needs no carve-out: the two declared outputs cite fixtures by ID and never echo an admitted symbol name, so B5 sweeps the run's FULL output tree — the declared outputs included — with no exclusion at all. Refused names are not admitted names and may be quoted. Without this rule B5's own clause would have to be read down to mean 'except my own evidence' before the gate could pass.

gates.B1: Over the sealed fixtures AND a machine-enumerated input sweep (every fixture line mutated by single-token deletion/substitution from the fixture alphabet — an enumerated set, not an authored one): 100% receive exactly one verdict with exactly one `deciding_clause`, zero fall-throughs.
gates.B2: Zero admissions collide with any member of the committed `symbol_census.json` (the checker compares against the committed artifact; the census *checker*, a separate invocation, proves the artifact matches a fresh recomputation — two sides, two programs, so a mismatch can actually go red). The `sum_total` fixture must refuse `RESERVED_PREFIX`; a fixture head equal to a casefolded corpus call head must refuse `COLLIDES_WITH_LIBRARY_SYMBOL`.
gates.B3: ≥30 seeded mutants attempt to move an admitted symbol into a rendered answer's evidence, a written session document, a journal, or a library path. 100% are stopped by the shipped machinery or the checker — not by test assertions reading the mutant's name. One survivor fails the slice.
gates.B4: `write_stage.working_tree_digest` is byte-identical before and after the full registered run (excluding the run's own declared output paths, named in the prereg); `durable_digest` over `data/` is the narrow named control. Zero stage records exist.
gates.B5: No written session document, journal, or durable artifact from the run contains any admitted fixture symbol name (swept over the run's full output tree); `session_state.encode` refuses both record types; a fresh session's use of an admitted fixture symbol takes the opaque-atom path (the declaration is gone).
gates.B6: Every fixture use of a declared symbol with wrong arity refuses `USE_ARITY_MISMATCH` naming the declaration; every fixture use of an *undeclared* applied atom produces byte-identical behavior to the same line on a tip without this slice (the regression fence, checked by replaying those lines against both code paths).
gates.B7: the machine-enumerated B1 sweep must hit at least 6 of the 8 refusal codes without any sweep input having been authored toward a code; a code reachable only by hand-crafted fixtures is reported by name in the artifact. All-admitted or all-UNPARSED on the sweep is BLOCKED CONSTRUCTION.
gates.B8: Remove one member from a copy of the census: the fixture admission that member blocked must flip to admitted (the freshness verdict moves). Remove one category from a copy of the schema enum: every fixture declaration citing that category must flip to `CATEGORY_NOT_IN_SCHEMA`. Both mutations name their target fixture in the prereg.
gates.B9: A surface-only admitter (token count, line length, presence of the command word; no census, no schema, no ledger) is fitted on a held-out half of the fixture corpus and scored on the other half, on the 2-valued verdict. The threshold is anchored to the scored half's majority-class rate, with a declared ten-point margin (a bound, not a measurement).
gates.B10: Fixtures, mutants, census, budget, and digests commit before the checker runs them; the run artifact cites the sealed commit; a dirty or wrong-tip tree refuses.
gates.B11: The import-closure assertion over the checker and ledger, in the `echo_population_audit` pattern.
gates.B12: for every admitted fixture symbol, declare then use, and assert the surface the use-side checker resolves is byte-identical to the ledger key. Mutants for this gate are seeded specifically at reserved-prefix-adjacent names.

frozen_numbers_note: The 8/3/4 floors, B3's 30, B7's 6-of-8 and B9's ten-point margin are DECLARED CONSTRUCTION BOUNDS, NOT MEASUREMENTS. B9's anchor was recomputed and re-sealed PRE-RUN when amendment 1 moved the declaration population 38 -> 39; the superseded anchor is recorded in the fixtures artifact's amendments block.

b8_named_targets.note: Both mutations are applied to COPIES held in memory; the committed census and the committed schema are never written. The target fixtures are named HERE, before the run, which is what B8 asks the prereg to do.

b9_control.split_rule: Enumerate the declaration fixtures in this artifact's sealed `fixtures` order, 0-based. Even index -> FIT half; odd index -> SCORED (held-out) half. Deterministic, committed before any admitter exists, and recomputable from these bytes alone.
b9_control.voiding_sentence: if the surface-only admitter's out-of-half agreement with the checker exceeds the scored half's majority-class rate by more than ten points, the verdict is separable from every ledger and schema input, the capability is void, and the slice ships as an honest negative.
b9_control.equality_note: The sentence says EXCEEDS by more than ten points. Agreement exactly equal to the threshold does not fire, and the runner records that explicitly rather than leaving a strict-vs-loose comparison to be read off code.

r_h1_sentence: A person can declare a fresh relation symbol with arity and argument categories; the system admits it into a session-scoped ledger or refuses with one deciding clause, totally; a misused declared symbol is refused by name where yesterday it was opaque text; and nothing declared survives the session or touches the library.
r_h1_requires_note: DESIGN §8 gates R-H1 on B1-B11 in its own words. B12 was added by the 2026-08-31 refinement round after §8's sentence was written; it is scored and reported beside them. The runner does not silently widen R-H1's requirement list, and a red B12 would be reported in the artifact rather than folded into R-H1 — stated here, before the score, so neither reading can be chosen after it.

r_h2.arm: run the 30 sealed inbound hypotheses through the declaration parser and count how many parse as declarations at all
r_h2.precommitted_reading: Approximately zero is the expected result and is neither a failure (the capability never claimed to serve those questions) nor evidence of demand — the number may not be read either way after the fact.

r_h3: Any failed construction gate B1-B8/B10/B11 or a fired B9 licenses the bounded negative with its verdict table; it does not license loosening a clause after the score.
b5_scope_sentence: This evidences NO WRITES OBSERVED UNDER THIS HARNESS, never CANNOT WRITE. The standing SURVIVES-with-scope rule from the v0.24 deep triage applies: the verdict travels with the harness that produced it.
amendments_note: Every entry below was authored on 2026-09-02, AFTER commit 2ac8c9f scored H-P1's first registered run and AFTER an independent adversarial review of that run returned MERGE AFTER FIXES. That ordering is the first thing each entry states, because an amendment written after a score is only admissible if it cannot move the score. NOTHING BELOW LOOSENS ANYTHING: no threshold, no floor, no clause text and no gate requirement list is edited, and no frozen row is rewritten in place. What the amendments add is disclosure, two live detectors where run 1 had checks that could not fail, and one repair to the committed tree. Run 1's artifacts are retained under experiments/superseded/ and are never re-scored.

amendments.finding: Review finding F3. B9's control family was never registered in this preregistration — it lived in the runner's code — and on the sealed corpus it is STRUCTURALLY UNABLE TO FIRE: the best agreement any member reaches on the 19-row scored half is 0.736842 against a void threshold of 0.784211. The fitted rule `line_length:eq:28` additionally predicts REFUSED for every scored row, which is why its agreement equals the majority-class rate exactly. Neither fact was disclosed in run 1's artifact.

registers_the_family_that_was_already_sc.shape: every rule `feature OP value` for feature in {token count, line length, presence of the command word} and OP in {le, ge, eq}, plus the two constant predictors ADMITTED and REFUSED
registers_the_family_that_was_already_sc.threshold_values_enumerated_over: the whole declaration corpus, disclosed in run 1 as leakage in the control's favour
registers_the_family_that_was_already_sc.tie_break: highest fit-half accuracy, then the lexicographically smallest rule id
registers_the_family_that_was_already_sc.note: written down here for the first time. It is the family run 1 scored, transcribed without change: registering it after the fact does not make it a pre-registered family, and this entry says so rather than implying otherwise.

adds_a_richer_family_as_a_reported_arm.shape: closed intervals lo <= feature <= hi on one of the same three allowed features, and conjunctions of two such intervals on two DIFFERENT features
adds_a_richer_family_as_a_reported_arm.fitted_on: the FIT half only, values enumerated from the fit half only
adds_a_richer_family_as_a_reported_arm.tie_break: highest fit-half accuracy; then the NARROWEST rule, measured as the sum of (hi - lo) over its interval clauses; then the lexicographically smallest rule id. Declared here and in the runner BEFORE the fit, so a fit-half tie is never resolved by a scored-half number — which is the leak the review named when it observed that an interval rule ties on the fit half and reaches 0.789474 out of half.
adds_a_richer_family_as_a_reported_arm.reported_as: `construction_gate.B9.richer_family.fit_half_selected` — whatever it says, including if it exceeds 0.784211 — beside `richer_family.ceiling_on_scored_half`, which is EXPLICITLY LABELLED as selection on the scored half and is not a control score.

amendments.what_decides_the_gate: B9's verdict, `voiding_sentence.fired`, and R-H1's `green` are all computed from the REGISTERED family and from nothing else, because the registered control is what this preregistration names and a control chosen after a result is not a control. If the richer family's fit-half-selected rule exceeds the threshold, the artifact records `voiding_sentence.fired_under_richer_family: true` and R-H1 carries a caveat naming it — the caveat travels with the sentence, and the sentence is not withdrawn by a family authored after the score.
amendments.what_a_successor_must_do: fix the control family, its tie-break and its threshold BEFORE its run, and score them on a held-out half larger than nineteen rows. Both findings here are findings about a family and a corpus size, not about the checker: a control that cannot fire measures nothing, and a nineteen-row half moves 0.0526 per row.
amendments.loosens_nothing: b9_void_threshold, b9_scored_half_majority_class_rate, b9_declared_margin_points, the voiding sentence and equality_is_not_a_firing are unchanged.

amendments.finding: Review finding F5. `sealed_commit_note` above says the H-PRE commit sealed experiments/house_rules_fixtures.json before scripts/symbol_ledger.py existed. That is true of the FILE and not of the PINNED BYTES: the corpus was first committed at 7a47a8a and its bytes last moved at e3e3980. Two commits moved them: c87b0ca rewrote the two `generator` fields when the builder moved into scripts/, and e3e3980 added the fixture hr-fx-s1-t14 together with the corpus's own `amendments` block and the B9 re-anchoring that addition forced. Run 1's artifact surfaced neither the amendments block nor the distinction.
amendments.corrects: the FRAMING of `sealed_commit_note`, which is NOT edited in place. B10's ancestry claim is unaffected and is exactly what the note's second sentence says: the sealed commit must be a strict ancestor of the scoring tip, and it is.
amendments.amendments_are_pre_run: Both corpus amendments predate any registered run: no checker had scored a verdict against this corpus when they were made, which is the only window the corpus's own amendment note permits it to move in.
amendments.the_re_anchoring_did_not_rescue_b9: Corpus amendment 1 moved the declaration population 38 -> 39 and re-anchored B9 from 0.731579 to 0.784211. The fitted rule is unfired against BOTH: 0.684211 does not exceed 0.731579 either. The run artifact reports this as `construction_gate.B9.superseded_anchor_arm`.
amendments.requires_of_the_run_artifact: a `corpus_provenance` block carrying the corpus's amendments block, `fixtures_first_committed_at` and `fixtures_pinned_bytes_committed_at`.
amendments.loosens_nothing: no frozen row, digest or number moves.

amendments.finding: Review findings F1, F2 and F4. (F1) B3 never executes a mutant: the 32 sealed mutants are prose descriptions, the id-to-detector map is authored in the runner, and run 1 never compared that map against each mutant's sealed `stopper_mechanism`. (F2) Two detectors could not fail — `name_sweep` planted a name in a temporary directory and found it, carrying seven mutants, and `checker_inputs_exclude_the_runs_outputs` asserted an absence true of every module that never mentions the run's outputs. (F4) The served `declare` grammar example carried an ADMITTED fixture symbol from H-P0 through run 1, which is b3-m08's own vector present in the committed tree while run 1 scored that mutant STOPPED.
requires_of_the_run_artifact: `detector_map_is_authored: true`, with each row carrying its sealed `stopper_mechanism` beside the detector mapped to it
a published keyword table mapping mechanism CLASSES to the phrases that identify them, and a per-mutant report of every class the seal names and whether the mapped detector's class is one of them
`detector_coverage_counts`, so no prose number about how many mutants a detector carries can drift
any mutant with no live detector reported as NOT COVERED BY A LIVE DETECTOR, with B3's stopped count dropping accordingly against the unchanged floor of 30

amendments.tree_repair: scripts/serve_chat.py's `declare` example is changed to a placeholder verified absent from the census, the schema and the whole fixture corpus, and experiments/session_p1_command_bound.json is regenerated by scripts/measure_command_bound.py. amendments.what_b3_still_cannot_claim: containment MEASURED. No mutant is executed by this run or by any program in this repository; the gate observes that each mapped detector fires on live material, and the artifact says so in the first field a reader meets. A successor that wants containment measured needs executable mutants.
amendments.loosens_nothing: b3_mutant_floor stays 30, b3_mutants_sealed stays 32, the B3 clause text is unchanged, and a detector that does not fire still fails every mutant mapped to it.

amendments.finding: Review findings F6, F7, F8, F12, F13, F14 and F15 — seven items that are disclosure or check-strength and move no number a gate reads.

requires_of_the_run_artifact.F6: B5's whole-repository disclosure called its hits 'the sealed corpus, its builder, and the H-P0 tests'; at least ten of twenty-one were none of those. The gloss is replaced by a published mechanical classification of every disclosed path. The per-path ADMITTED NAME is deliberately NOT published: this artifact is inside the swept tree, so the honest table would make B5 red by the act of disclosing.
requires_of_the_run_artifact.F7: the artifact publishes `provenance.second_program.covers` and `.does_not_cover`; seven of the twelve gates are scored once and the artifact says which.
requires_of_the_run_artifact.F8: B6's regression fence gains the POPULATED-ledger arm; the empty-ledger arm is kept and labelled as the trivial one, because check_use returns None on an empty table and the two paths provably agree.
requires_of_the_run_artifact.F12: B2's `admissions: 17` is relabelled `admitted_names_swept` with `live_admissions` beside it and the union explained.
requires_of_the_run_artifact.F13: `mutation_covers_the_command_word`, `sweep.authored_toward_a_code` and `no_sweep_input_authored_toward_a_code` are COMPUTED from the sweep rather than hardcoded, and the fixture alphabet is pinned by digest.
requires_of_the_run_artifact.F14: B12's mutant arm resolves against the LIVE ledger key, as the pairs arm already did; agreement with the seal is reported separately.
requires_of_the_run_artifact.F15: the receipt checker's `unreadable-<artifact>` failure gains a tamper test.

amendments.loosens_nothing: every threshold, floor, clause and requirement list is unchanged; B6 and B7 gain checks that can fail and lose none.

amendments.finding: Review finding F11. `registered_date` above reads 2026-09-01 while the commit that first added this file, 27d358d, is dated 2026-09-02.
amendments.reconciliation: The registration was authored and its numbers fixed on 2026-09-01, in the same working session as H-P0's fix commit e3e3980; it was committed early on 2026-09-02. The field is NOT edited: it records when the registration was written, the commit records when it entered the history, and B10's ancestry proof reads the commit and never the field. The two are reconciled here rather than made to agree.

non_claims: ledger-groundedness, never correspondence: an admitted declaration is well-formed and fresh, never true or useful
no axioms or premises about declared symbols, and no conservativity
no persistence, and no export toward library files
no behaviour on the served HTTP profiles beyond the published ¶DEV-1 note
no claim about what people will declare once they can
